gaps.quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$
gaps.note: The cited fact is about scalar banks x_S, y_S indexed by triples S (paper lines 729-737, Lemma scalar-motifs), where a forward invocation sends y_S to y_S+x_S. The shear H <- H+D is an address permutation of fields of an array, not an addition of bank scalars. The page never says how D and H are identified with the banks X and Y; in the paper the shear is obtained by applying Phi_M to role streams and merging (lines 1495-1534), and exactness for arbitrary scratch rows follows from that. Also the exchange of banks is only (X,Y) -> (-Y,X) in general, and an exact exchange only in the bit construction (line 735-738), which the page does not state.

The page never says what mu is for the explicit network (paper line 656: m = 1000000), so the bound mu < 2^20 is unsupported and not marked cited; the step to ln mu < 20 also uses ln 2 < 1 (paper line 1332), which is not stated.

gaps.quote: The outer two cost linear time.
gaps.note: No reason is given why D <- D-H and D <- H-D take linear time on a tape. The paper (line 1539-1541) relies on the ordered affine stream lemma: they update a later field from an earlier field in one pass. The page does not state or cite this.

gaps.quote: Splitting, merging and gates are a fixed number of linear passes, $O(1)$ per unit volume.
gaps.note: The recurrence F_d <= lambda F_{d-1} + O(1) also needs the cost of scheduling the s recursive calls on a fixed number of tapes (parking stack, descriptor stack) to be O(V) at each node; the paper proves this separately (lines 1560-1620). The page omits it, so the recurrence is not justified from what is given.
